The error indicates that it can't find the fortran compiler, so the problem is with how you're installing fortran " /opt/gfortran/bin/gfortran: No such file or directory"
Googling that error I got to this page <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69639782/installing-gfortran-on-macbook-with-apple-m1-chip-for-use-in-r> which you can have a look at and try out or see if you can find other solutions.
All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: era5 download issues
messages.body_plain:
Hi Liang,

Sorry I missed your latest response. Yes, although I haven't experimented much with areas as large as you have requested here (ie -90 to 90 latitude), I imagine this will exceed quotas that the Climate Data Store allows for a single request. Furthermore mcera5 isn't designed to download such large swathes of the planet at once. You'd be better off iterating through smaller areas, to start!

Best,
Dave
ᐧ
ᐧ

Liang

On Monday, December 11, 2023 at 11:06:50 PM UTC+8 dkli...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Liang,
>
> Sorry I missed your latest response. Yes, although I haven't experimented much with areas as large as you have requested here (ie -90 to 90 latitude), I imagine this will exceed quotas that the Climate Data Store allows for a single request. Furthermore mcera5 isn't designed to download such large swathes of the planet at once. You'd be better off iterating through smaller areas, to start!
>
> Best,
> Dave
> ᐧ
> ᐧ
>
> On Mon, Nov 20, 2023 at 5:58 PM Liang Ma <mayin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Dave,
> >
> > Sorry for the late response! I asked the question and then went out of town for two conferences, so much so that I forgot I asked the question!
> >
> > My input values for build_era5_request() was:
> > build_era5_request(xmin = -180, xmax = -175,
> >                             ymin = -90, ymax = 90,
> >                             start_time = "2022-01-01",
> >                             end_time = "2022-01-01",
> >                             outfile_name = "-180_-175")
> > Actually, I was trying to do this in a for loop and download the global era5 data for 2022 at intervals of 5 degrees of longitude (I have done so for the year 2019). I wonder if it is because I have downloaded too much era5 data with my account, so I am not allowed to continue to download data in batches.
> >
> > Looking forward to your advice. Thank you very much for the help!
> >
> > All the best,
> >
> > Liang

> > >
> > > Sorry to hear that you've had troubles. Could you send me the input values for build_era5_request() that you attempted to use? It seems from the name of your requested file ("-180_-175_2022.nc <https://streaklinks.com/Bt4HIMop6VUxsqjKaQ5OEfKJ/http%3A%2F%2F180_-175_2022.nc>") that you have xmn = -180, xmx = -175, and some part or all of year 2022, but the function also requires ymn and ymax.

> > > xmx

> > > > I haven't had a successful download of era5 in recent months. It always froze at:

> > > >
> > > > My ecmwfr version was 1.5.0.
> > > >
> > > > The code I used for downloading is:
> > > >     req<-build_era5_request(xmin = xmn, xmax = xmx,

> > > >
> > > > Liang
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Wednesday, November 9, 2022 at 10:44:57 AM UTC+8 dkli...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > Hi André,
> > > > >
> > > > > If by model you mean the NicheMapR microclimate model, yes most of the NicheMapR wrapper functions that leverage the microclimate model have some option to save downloaded climate and re-access the local data, or you can modify one of the wrapper functions to access a custom climate dataset (from experience this may take a bit of effort). However I want to note that for all of the NicheMapR wrapper functions– including micro_era5 that uses mcera5– once you download the climate dataset once, if you set save = 1 then the climate forcing data will be saved (setting save = 2 will access saved climate data). For downloading ERA5 data via mcera5, I want to note that the download times are mostly due to the CDS API server, which is out of control of mcera5 and will be the case no matter what fashion you download CDS data. But, once downloaded, you won't need to do so again for the same time and place.
> > > > >
> > > > > Best,
> > > > > Dave

They should be listed there.
